rows.ts_value: New $3,000,000,000 five-year senior unsecured multicurrency revolving facility (borrow, repay and reborrow) for general corporate purposes. It replaces and refinances the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements (2021 and 2023 Citibank-agented revolvers). The TS dates Amendment No. 2 to the 2023 Credit Agreement February 16, 2024. The $4bn acquisition term loan sits under a separate term sheet and is not part of this facility.

rows.ca_value: New standalone Credit Agreement dated as of September 18, 2026, not an amendment. Single revolving facility: Borrowers may borrow, repay and reborrow (s.2.1). No term loan tranche. Effectiveness requires the commitments under the Existing 2021 and 2023 Credit Agreements to be terminated and repaid (s.4.1(i)). The CA definition of "Existing 2023 Credit Agreement" dates Amendment No. 2 April 16, 2024.

One drafting inconsistency: the TS dates Amendment No. 2 to the 2023 Credit Agreement February 16, 2024, but the CA dates it April 16, 2024. The refinanced agreements are clearly the same, so the economics are unaffected.

Request window: no earlier than 60 and no later than 30 days before the anniversary. Lenders respond 20 days before; Agent notifies the Parent 15 days before. The extension is effective only if more than 50% of the Facility Amount is extended or committed. Declining Lenders keep their existing date and may be replaced by third parties reasonably acceptable to the Agent. No term-out option.

Lender election by a Notice Date 20 days before; Agent notice 15 days before. Effective only if more than 50% of the Aggregate Commitment is extended or assumed. Non-Extending Lenders keep their prior date and may be replaced by Eligible Assignees. Lenders that do not respond are deemed Non-Extending. Subject to the s.4.5 conditions. No term-out option.

The CA has the Borrower Representative (Aon NA) make the request instead of the Parent, and it treats lenders that do not respond as Non-Extending. Both are mechanical differences.

rows.ts_value: Parent may increase the Facility Amount after the Revolving Effective Date, no more than once a year, in minimum increments of $10,000,000, by up to $1,800,000,000 (total $4.8bn). Conditions: representations true and no Default or Event of Default. The increase may be offered to existing lenders (allocations set by the Parent and the Agent) or to third parties, each committing at least $5,000,000. The TS conditions for Commitment Increases are "Limited to" representations and no default.
rows.ts_quote: The Parent will have the right after the Revolving Effective Date, no more than once a year, to increase the Facility Amount, in minimum increments of $10,000,000, up to a maximum amount of $1,800,000,000
rows.ts_location: PDF p.3, Commitment Increase; PDF p.9, Conditions Precedent to Advances, Commitment Increases and Commitment Extensions
rows.ca_value: Borrower Representative may request increases no more than once per calendar year, in $10,000,000 or integral multiples of it. Total Commitments are capped at $4,800,000,000 at any time. The increase must take effect at least 30 days before the latest scheduled Facility Termination Date. Eligible Assignees must commit at least $5,000,000. Where the increase is oversubscribed, allocation is agreed by the Borrower Representative in consultation with the Agent. Conditions in s.4.4: no Default or Unmatured Default, and representations true. Under s.2.19(a)(ii) the Article IV conditions must be met on both the request date and the Increase Date. On the Increase Date the Agent must also receive certified board resolutions of each Loan Party and an opinion of counsel (which may be in-house counsel) under s.2.19(c)(i).
rows.ca_quote: in no event shall the aggregate amount of the Commitments at any time exceed $4,800,000,000
rows.explanation: The economics match: a $1.8bn increase on $3.0bn equals the CA's $4.8bn cap, and the $5m minimum per new lender is the same. The TS says the conditions for an increase are "Limited to" representations and no default, but the CA adds board resolutions, a legal opinion, testing of the conditions on the request date as well, a 30-day cut-off before maturity, and increases in integral multiples of $10m rather than a $10m minimum. Smaller differences: the limit is once per calendar year, and the Borrower Representative decides the allocation after consulting the Agent instead of deciding it jointly with the Agent. Because the CA caps total Commitments rather than the amount of increases, a borrower that has reduced its commitments could add more than $1.8bn in total. That point favours the borrower, but lenders never have to take part.

rows.attribute: Benchmark rates, floors and credit spread adjustment
rows.ts_value: USD: Alternate Base Rate or Term SOFR. EUR: EURIBOR. GBP: SONIA, defined as the daily rate published on the fifth business day before the relevant day. No credit spread adjustment. Floors are not stated. ABR, Term SOFR and EURIBOR take their meaning from the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements.
rows.ts_quote: The interest rates shall not include a credit spread adjustment.
rows.ca_value: ABR is the highest of the Citibank base rate, Federal Funds Effective Rate + 0.5% and 1-month Term SOFR + 1%. Term SOFR has a Floor of 0.00%. The EURIBO Rate (Eurocurrency Base Rate) is floored at zero and grossed up for the Reserve Requirement. SONIA uses the fifth-Business-Day lookback and is floored at zero. The Federal Funds Effective Rate is floored at zero. No CSA; a spread adjustment appears only in the benchmark replacement provisions (s.2.23). ABR, the Term SOFR Rate, the Eurocurrency Rate and SONIA are defined as all-in rates that include the Applicable Margin.
rows.ca_quote: provided that if Term SOFR as so determined shall ever be less than the Floor, then Term SOFR shall be deemed to be equal to the Floor.

rows.explanation: The benchmarks by currency, the absence of a CSA and the 5-business-day SONIA lookback all match. The CA adds 0% floors on every benchmark and a reserve gross-up on EURIBOR. The Term SOFR, EURIBOR and ABR floors may come from the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements, which were not provided. The SONIA floor cannot come from them, because the TS defines SONIA itself and gives it no floor.

In addition, during an insolvency Default under s.7.6 or 7.7 (voluntary or involuntary insolvency of any Loan Party or Significant Subsidiary), the default rates apply automatically, without notice, to ALL Credit Extensions. "continue" means until cured or waived.

The CA adds a trigger the TS does not have: an insolvency Default applies the 2% rate automatically to all outstanding Credit Extensions, not only overdue amounts. Sections 7.6 and 7.7 also cover the insolvency of any Significant Subsidiary, so the higher rate can apply even when the Obligations have not been accelerated. Automatic acceleration under s.8.1(a) applies only to US-organised Borrowers.

rows.ca_value: No amortization. All Obligations are due on the Facility Termination Date (s.2.2). Mandatory prepayment applies if, on a quarterly-or-more-frequent currency revaluation, total Advances exceed 103% of the Aggregate Commitment or Aon UK Limited Advances exceed 103% of the Aon UK Limited Sublimit. The excess must be repaid down to 100% within two Business Days of notice (s.2.7(b)). As drafted, limb (ii) adds all Dollar Advances to AUK's Committed Currency Advances.
rows.ca_quote: the Borrowers shall, as soon as practicable and in any event within two Business Days after receipt of such notice, prepay the outstanding principal amount of any Advances owing by the Borrowers
rows.explanation: The single payment at maturity matches. The CA adds a customary currency-fluctuation clean-down (a 103% trigger, repaid to 100%) that the TS does not state; the 3% headroom limits its effect. One drafting point should be confirmed: read literally, the AUK test in s.2.7(b)(i)(ii) counts all Dollar Advances to any Borrower, because "that are made to Aon UK Limited" follows only the Committed Currency part. That would force prepayments well beyond the TS sublimit. It is probably meant to count AUK Advances only.

TS: \"Summary of the Revolving Facility\" (marked \"Posting Version\"), an 11-page lender-facing summary of terms for Aon North America, Inc., Aon Corporation, Aon Global Holdings plc, Aon Global Limited and Aon UK Limited. It is undated but refers to the merger agreement dated August 30, 2026, and it states that its terms are not final. Schedule I (Pricing Grid) is on PDF p.11. The TS also mentions a separate $4.0bn acquisition term loan under a different term sheet; that term loan is out of scope here.

CA: a new standalone Credit Agreement (Execution Version, filed as Exhibit 10.2) dated as of September 18, 2026. It is not an amendment. Parties are Aon plc (Parent/Guarantor), the five named Borrowers, Citibank, N.A. as Administrative Agent and BofA Securities as Syndication Agent. It is a $3.0bn multicurrency revolving facility. CA PDF page numbers are the printed page number plus 6.

Limitations:
(1) Schedule 1 (Commitments) only says \"[On File with Administrative Agent]\" (PDF p.136), so individual lender allocations cannot be reconciled. Only the $3.0bn aggregate can be checked.
(2) The fee letters dated August 30, 2026 referred to in CA s.4.1(h) and s.10.10 were not provided, so upfront and arrangement fee amounts cannot be checked.
(3) The TS takes the definitions of Alternate Base Rate, Term SOFR and EURIBOR from the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements, which were not provided.
(4) The pricing grids in both text files are garbled. Grid values were re-read with pdftotext -raw on TS PDF p.11 and CA PDF p.135, and all 15 values matched. Quotes for the grid rows are taken from the narrative text below each table.
(5) X01 is an extra TS interest term (conversion of Term Rate Advances during an Event of Default) that is not on the checklist.

All ts_quote and ca_quote strings were checked mechanically (whitespace collapsed) and appear verbatim in the text files.

Observations outside group A, for the other groups:
(a) The TS says \"each Borrower shall be a Guarantor\" (PDF p.2), but the CA \"Guarantor\" definition (PDF p.20) states that Aon UK Limited is not a Guarantor as of the Effective Date.
(b) The CA names HSBC, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo as additional Joint Lead Arrangers. The TS allows for \"any Additional Arranger\".
(c) The CA excludes Designated Subsidiaries organised in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein or Norway; the TS excludes only EU Member States.

TS: "Summary of the Revolving Facility" (marked "Posting Version", undated; 11 PDF pages including the Schedule I pricing grid). It is a summary term sheet for a $3.0bn five-year revolving facility for Aon North America, Inc., Aon Corporation, Aon Global Holdings plc, Aon Global Limited and Aon UK Limited, with Aon plc as Parent. The facility is tied to the acquisition of USI Advantage Corp. under a merger agreement dated August 30, 2026, and to the refinancing of the 2021 and 2023 Existing Revolving Credit Agreements. Under its Documentation Principles, most legal terms only need to be "substantially similar/consistent" with the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements.

CA: a new, standalone Credit Agreement dated as of September 18, 2026 (Execution Version, filed as Exhibit 10.2; 161 PDF pages including exhibits and schedules). It is not an amendment, so the reconciliation is against this agreement as executed. The "Effective Date" is defined in s.4.1 as the date the conditions are satisfied, not as a fixed date. The agreement date and the September 18, 2031 Facility Termination Date are consistent with a September 18, 2026 Effective Date. In the CA body, PDF page numbers run 6 ahead of the printed page numbers (printed p.54 = PDF p.60). All page references here are PDF pages.

Limitations:
(1) Schedule 1 (Commitments) reads "[On File with Administrative Agent]" (PDF p.136), so individual lender allocations cannot be checked. Loan Party signature pages are PDF pp.111-112, and lender identities come from the lender signature pages, PDF pp.113-134.
(2) The Existing Revolving Credit Agreements were not provided. Items the TS fixes only by reference to them (assignments, yield protection, indemnity, related covenant definitions, basket sizes) are checked for consistency with the TS wording only, not against the existing agreements.
(3) The TS text extraction is two-column and garbled: on PDF pp.3-4, 6, 8 and 10 the heading labels are pulled out of line with their text. Headings were mapped to text by sequence. For example, on p.8 "Use of proceeds; merger; liens; affiliates; change in fiscal year; and indebtedness" is the Negative Covenants text, and on p.10 the two "substantially consistent" sentences are Yield Protection and Indemnity, in that order. Neither the original analyst nor the reviewer could render the PDFs as images to confirm this, because pdftoppm is not installed. The sequence mapping is consistent with the heading order on each page.
(4) The CA also contains standard provisions the TS does not mention: EU/UK bail-in (s.9.14), erroneous payments (s.10.12), lender ERISA representations (s.10.11), benchmark replacement (s.2.23), Disqualified Lenders (s.12.6) and a 20% cap on any one lender's commitment (s.12.2). These are noted where relevant, but because the TS does not state them they get no separate X rows.
(5) The reviewer added X12 (availability, borrowing mechanics and currencies) and X13 (voluntary commitment reductions). These are TS terms that are not on the Group A topic list; drop them if Group A already covers them.

Group A economic terms (amount, pricing, fees, maturity, accordion, extensions, sublimits, prepayments, interest mechanics, default interest and post-default rate conversion) are excluded under the task split.
